preamble: De-retroflexion of the voiceless retroflex affricate [ʈʂ] to alveolar [ts] merges the retroflex and dental sibilant series. In colloquial Taiwanese Mandarin, Standard Mandarin zh- is pronounced as z- in most contexts. Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties, including Chengdu Sichuanese, have lost the retroflex series and merged zh, ch and sh with z, c and s, so Middle Chinese 莊 tsrjang and 爭 tsreang (Baxter) are Chengdu zuang1 and zen1. Polish mazurzenie (cz > c) is filed under tʃ > ts, since Koneczna and the description Wikipedia gives after Dejna, Kuraszkiewicz and Rospond derive the mazurating dentals directly from the older palato-alveolars.

languageExamples.language: Taiwanese Mandarin: Standard Guoyu zh- [ʈʂ] ~ colloquial Taiwan Guoyu z- [ts] (correspondence)

examples.note: Colloquial Taiwan Guoyu pronounces zh-, ch- and sh- like z-, c- and s- in most contexts. Wikipedia (Taiwanese Mandarin) calls the merger "nonstandard, [but] extremely common across all Mandarin speakers in Taiwan, even the highly educated"; Standard Guoyu keeps the retroflex series.
The same merger applies to every zh- syllable.

Baxter's tsr- is the retroflex sibilant affricate of the 莊 initial (Pan Wuyun and Pulleyblank /ʈ͡ʂ/; Zhengzhang reconstructs /t͡ʃ/). Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties have lost the retroflex series, merging it with the alveolar affricates and fricatives.

examples.from: 爭 tsreang 'to contend', 斬 tsreamX 'to chop' (Baxter)
examples.note: Both have the 莊 initial; Standard Mandarin keeps the retroflex (zhēng, zhǎn).

examples.to: Old Georgian ცჳლი cwli, Georgian ცვილი cvili

examples.note: Georgian c [t͡s] continues the subscript-1 affricate, which Zan and Svan reflect as č. Wiktionary's subscript-1 series (*s₁, *z₁, *c₁, *ʒ₁) is the Gamkrelidze-Machavariani 'hissing-hushing' series, given in the Wikipedia Proto-Kartvelian consonant table (after Gamkrelidze 1966 and Fähnrich 2002) as retroflex [ʂ ʐ ʈ͡ʂ ɖ͡ʐ].
